chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbaat, from Ahmad ibn Umar al-Hallal, from Ali ibn Suweyd, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about the self-conceit that ruins the deed, so he said: 'Self-conceit has levels. One of them is that the evil of the servant's deed is adorned for him, so he sees it as good, so it astounds him and he reckons that he has done something good; and another is that the servant believes in his Lord, so he thinks he is doing a favour upon Allah, Mighty and Majestic, while for Allah, upon him with regards to it, is actually the Favour.'

key_terms.الْعُجْب: Self-conceit or pride in one's own deeds

ai.seo_question: What are the levels of self-conceit (al-'Ujb) that ruin good deeds according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) delineates self-conceit (al-'Ujb) as a spiritual disease that corrupts deeds by either distorting self-perception or causing the believer to 'count favors' upon God. This second form highlights a subtle arrogance where one views their faith as a gift bestowed upon the Divine, rather than recognizing it as God's immense grace upon the servant. This concept is central to Shia ethical theology, illustrating how even valid acts of worship can be nullified by the internal state of self-importance.
